problems.statement: The record FY2026 results are mainly a commodity price windfall, not evidence of operational excellence: revenue rose 46.5% on a 46% corn price rise with volume flat/down 0.9%, and the cooperative ranked mid-pack versus peers.

The headline KPI improvement (17.4 to 16.4 cents per bushel) is an artifact of deferred maintenance; excluding maintenance, other costs were flat (14.6 vs 14.5), and the maintenance cut produced a growing backlog.

Harlan Junction has a serious, unmanaged combustible-dust/ignition hazard (hot bearing, disabled sensors, dust accumulation, deferred safety work orders) with a looming insurer deadline of 21 Nov 2026.
The safety management system fails to learn: reporting works but near-misses are not investigated or acted on, and a policy-required investigation was skipped and closed with no root cause.
Incentives (GM bonus on revenue, dividends and cost per bushel, with no safety, maintenance or succession measure) plus the hiring freeze drive the cost-cutting at the expense of resilience.

Key-person dependency: dryer operation and grade blending at Harlan Junction and Wexford rest undocumented with one 63-year-old superintendent who plans to go part-time after 2027 and has no successor, no shadowing and no controlled procedures; the Harlan site's superior drying/grading performance is plausibly his skill rather than transferable systems.

The expansion proposal is built on fragile assumptions: baselined on a price-inflated FY2026, volume growth with no source, no downside or debt-service analysis, staffing and maintenance plans blank, and commissioning dependent on the retiring superintendent, while prices are expected to fall back.
The Operational Excellence program caused the record results and shows operations are ready to scale (the client's presented claim).
The Superintendent's presence causally explains the better drying/grade outcomes at his two sites versus older-equipment sites; equipment age is a confound (2019/2021 vs 1998/2001 dryers).

actions.action: Do not confirm operational readiness or write the readiness section as requested; tell the board the evidence contradicts it.
actions.rationale: Readiness claim rests on a price windfall and a cost KPI inflated by deferred maintenance.

actions.action: Immediately remediate Harlan Junction hazards (reconnect leg #2 sensor and offline monitors, baghouse, dust housekeeping, safety work orders) before the 21 Nov insurer deadline.
actions.rationale: Ignition and dust-explosion risk is live and there is a coverage and surcharge consequence.

actions.action: Reopen NM-26-007 as a documented investigation under SP-04 and audit all near-misses and closure practice.
actions.rationale: Mandatory policy was breached and the reporting system is not producing corrective action.

actions.action: Postpone the 15 December expansion vote until a stress-tested proposal exists (downside prices near $4.35 corn, debt-service coverage, volume source, staffing and maintenance plans).
actions.rationale: $15.7M debt on a windfall baseline with unsupported volume is a material member-wealth risk, and delay costs little.

actions.action: Fund and schedule the deferred maintenance backlog ($1.26M) and restate the cost KPI with maintenance normalized.
actions.rationale: The KPI is misleading and the backlog compounds risk.

actions.action: Start succession and knowledge capture for the Superintendent (shadowing, documented dryer and blend procedures), lift the freeze for the two assistant positions.
actions.rationale: Single-point-of-failure with retirement or part-time exit inside the project timeline.

actions.action: Revise GM and executive incentives to include safety, maintenance and succession measures and rebalance away from revenue and cost per bushel.
actions.rationale: Incentive design plausibly drives short-termism but the causal link is not proven.

actions.action: Give the GM and management personal credit for record results or reward them with the Operational Excellence-based bonus now.
actions.rationale: Results are price-driven and the cost KPI is gamed by deferral.

actions.action: Attribute the Harlan/Wexford quality advantage to the superintendent and replicate it by copying his role elsewhere without checking dryer age.
Proceed with the vote on 15 December on momentum with 'to follow' staffing and maintenance sections.
actions.rationale: Commits major debt with no downside analysis and an unresolved safety and insurance problem.

Insurer's corrective-action status and Harlan Junction hazard-monitoring, dust and bearing-sensor status; any other legs or equipment with similar bearing/vibration histories, and the reason for the disconnected sensor.
Peer or internal comparison of drying shrink and grade discounts controlling for dryer age and operator, plus timeline of the superintendent's succession and the documentation effort.
output.summary: The record year is mostly a commodity price windfall: revenue rose 46.5% on a 46% price rise with flat volume, and the cooperative ranks mid-pack among peers. The cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from deferred maintenance, leaving a backlog 3.1 times the FY2024 level and an unmanaged dust-ignition hazard at Harlan Junction. Near-miss investigations are skipped, the insurer's deadline is 21 November, and the hiring freeze and incentives reinforce the cost-cutting. Dryer and grading know-how sits with one retiring, undocumented superintendent. The expansion rests on a windfall baseline and has no downside analysis. Do not certify readiness; fix safety, then postpone the vote and stress-test the proposal.
